title: Characterization of Marker Molecules for the Diagnosis and Monitoring of Marginal Periodontitis 2.0
summary: In this study, dentists and researchers are investigating why some people respond poorly to treatment for periodontitis (gum disease). About 1,000 participants will provide samples such as saliva and blood, which will be analyzed in the lab. The goal is to find so-called biomarkers—measurable indicators—that can help predict how well a person will respond to therapy or how the disease might progress. This knowledge could help tailor future treatments more precisely to individual patients.
conditions: Disorder of teeth and supporting structures, unspecified

interventions.name:
Patients with periodontitis
500 participants will provide samples such as saliva and blood, which will be analyzed in the lab for several biomarker.

Periodontally healthy individuals
500 participants will provide samples such as saliva and blood, which will be analyzed in the lab for several biomarker.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age: ≥ 18 years
General health: ASA classification 1 or 2 (healthy or mildly ill)
Written informed consent
Additionally:

Group 1: Diagnosed periodontitis
Group 2 (control group): Periodontally healthy individuals
Exclusion criteria:
Under 18 years of age
Poor general health (ASA classification ≥ 3)
Unable to give informed consent
Acute inflammatory diseases outside the oral cavity
No written consent
Fewer than 10 teeth
Pregnancy
Diseases with immunosuppression or ongoing immunosuppressive therapy
Increased risk of infectious endocarditis
Increased risk of medication-induced jaw necrosis
